headline: Clinton order sets out how federal agencies carry out two 2000 trade laws covering sub-Saharan Africa and the Caribbean Basin.
what_it_does: This executive order deals with putting into practice the African Growth and Opportunity Act and the United States-Caribbean Basin Trade Partnership Act. Both laws give certain goods from eligible countries in those regions easier access to the US market. The order appears to assign tasks to federal agencies to run these programs. No summary was provided, so the exact duties and agencies involved are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses in eligible sub-Saharan African and Caribbean Basin countries
who_it_affects.how: The order relates to how the US runs the trade benefits these businesses can use when selling goods to the United States.

who_it_affects.group: US companies that import goods from these regions
who_it_affects.how: How the programs are carried out may affect the rules these importers follow to get trade benefits.
The order likely gives these agencies specific jobs in running the two trade laws.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed January 17, 2001; executive orders usually take effect when signed.
